text: People own graphs: one-click graph on a host, links between graphs, one global graph across servers
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: "that actually comes closest to the reality: People owning graphs. Everyone can make a proposal which is his graph. And then ideally the website would be able to access different servers (almost like federated)." The hurdle to participate is too high today: you have to set up a repo. "If we could make that simple and one-click, that'd be awesome. Then the result would really be a global ever expanding graph of ideas. aimparency. ideaparency. global. I'd love this."

Felix 2026-11-12, later, decided ("I love love love how this is coming together"):
- Checking out other people's graphs locally is the problem. Everyone hosts their own graph or uses something that hosts it.
- A link points for sure to the Aimparency server hosting the graph, maybe also to the repo.
- Servers allow requests from other origins, so the web app can follow links everywhere and expand sub-graphs into other servers.
- For Commons Hub: a server where people host their graphs or mirror GitHub repos (at least the .bowman part), so that people can view them.
- The guest layer stays (34b3d747): people add notes; configurable in the Aimparency server per graph: everyone, or only selected accounts. Accounts can also be granted write access.

What led here (2026-11-11): every design that put all people into one graph needed rules for who may touch which idea (owners and levels per idea, signed commits, a GitHub check) and felt cumbersome or like a compromise. Here the unit of ownership is the graph.

Relation to the standing decision of 2026-06-27 and 2026-09-20 (e81b11c3, links only to a whole graph, which stays a black box): expanding a linked graph in the web app shows its ideas, which a82b1530 ruled out. Noted by Claude, not confirmed by Felix: the stored link can stay graph-level while the browser loads the other graph on demand from its own server.

Exists today: an idea supported by a whole linked repo, drawn as one node with value flow (e81b11c3); opening any graph from a Git URL read-only in the normal UI as a shallow clone of .bowman only (250fb1aa, 9beb3725); spinning a branch off into its own graph (10a0561b); hosted mode with read, write and admin accounts and a read-only mode, for one project per server (af701cd6).

Missing, not designed: a server that holds many graphs, each with its own address and access settings, hosted or mirrored; creating a graph there in one click, without a repo; linking to a graph by server address instead of a local checkout; the offer side of a link (a graph says which idea of another graph it supports, with a pitch) and its acceptance; the web app loading a graph from another server.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: With many graphs on one server, a person gets a graph without setting up a repo or a server of their own.
When an account appears without a form, people act on a graph the moment they open it, and still can keep the account later.
Rights per graph instead of per idea are enough for people to work together, and simple enough to understand without explanation.
A link by server address can be followed by anyone from anywhere, so graphs on different servers join into one.
When a linked graph opens in place, people experience the graphs of many owners on many servers as one graph.
When proposing is the same gesture as adding an idea, people who cannot write to a graph still contribute to it, with a graph of their own.
With these limits, opening a server to anyone does not put the server, its graphs or its agents at risk.
When a person can connect an agent to chosen graphs in one approval step, agents work on hosted graphs without receiving more rights than the task needs.

status.comment: Decided by Felix as the direction on 2026-11-12 and planned in parts the same day: many graphs on one server (548c5b94), accounts (383e8949), access per graph (8faf6a70), proposing (b7e0b972), safety (8a303626), links by host URL (96d638bf), the web app across servers (588568b7). First use: Hack the Hub in December 2026 (96e9fc41). Nothing built yet. Felix: this implicitly solves the scaling problem, and it is like intention-connections between open-source repos. Cancelled as replaced: fcb38df6, 698badcb, b9744739.
